excerpts.text: Each capability call carries a structural identity built from its callsite, its fanout position, and its occurrence count
The frozen unit is the call expression, and the surrounding code stays writable.
A static gate rejects a rewrite that would change a committed call before a container starts.
A runtime digest stops a changed payload at a committed identity
Reachability and the payload digest are separate checks, because neither can be decided from the source.
A data-dependent payload edit preserves both and is caught by the runtime digest at dispatch.
The gate catches source-level drift, and the digest catches value-level drift.
so callsite identity turns a relocation into a pre-spend stop.
Inserting a fanout branch ahead of a committed one moves every later branch by one path index.
Two committed identities become orphans and the run otherwise succeeds.
We keep warn as the default because an orphan is a fidelity event
Storage errors are fail-closed by default
The implementation is Python 3.11, and the run store is SQLite in WAL mode.
The prototype runs the contract inside a networkless Docker sandbox that never sees a provider credential.
A host service accepts a model-authored script as a job
Our guarantee is identity-level, and it covers the calls that a candidate keeps and the identities that it invokes.

number_hygiene.policy: Paper empirical numbers are not targets or claims of this sketch. They may appear only here and as ABSENT-needles in tests.
number_hygiene.paper_sentence_FOUND: 22 gate-passed repairs replay 258 committed identities with no duplicate, and a live six-way fanout makes seven paid calls instead of twelve

modelling_note: Toy model: callsite path = enclosing function + block kind/ordinal path + ordinal of ctx.run in the innermost block; fanout index pushed by ctx.fanout; occurrence counter per (callsite, path). Call-expression fingerprint = sha256 of ast.dump of the ctx.run call. Payload digest = sha256 of canonical JSON. Ledger is a JSON fixture. Orphan policy warn (default) / stop applied after a completed run, as the paper describes; a stopped run's not-invoked identities are reported as unreached, not orphans. The occurrence ledger is reduced to a same-(site,path,digest) check with warn/stop/auto policy. Sequential toy fanout, so a path shift stops before any dispatch here (the paper's concurrent run may differ).
